name: World Significance / TED & Global Media Readiness
purpose: Continuously develop the evidence-backed World_server capabilities that can justify serious international media coverage and conference-stage applications.
interpretation: This is readiness of the project to support a credible world-scale story and reproducible public demonstration. It is NOT a probability of acceptance by TED, TEDx, a conference, or a media outlet.
formula: weighted mean of 12 system readiness values; weights sum to 100
antiInflation: Documentation, plans, prompts, labels, elapsed time, and self-asserted claims do not increase readiness.
Every positive readiness delta must cite new implementation, test, runtime, replay, independent review, live evidence, external reproduction, or measured user evidence.
Regression or invalidated evidence may reduce readiness.
UNKNOWN is preferred to invented precision.
Cross-system synergy changes prioritization, not score directly.
A system cannot exceed 60 without runtime evidence, 80 without independent exact-revision verification, or 95 without repeatable external/public reproduction evidence.
Novelty claims must not use 'first in the world' without fresh prior-art research and an exact narrowly scoped claim.

mutualReinforcement.rule: Prefer bounded vertical slices that strengthen two or more systems through one shared implementation, while preserving one primary bottleneck per run.
examples: event log + deterministic replay strengthens Eternal World, Shared Causal World, Provenance/Replay, Experiment Engine and Media Demo
typed free intent + causal engine strengthens Free Intent Compiler, Causal Engine, Recipe Standard and Media Demo
two-user continuation + durable event lineage strengthens Shared Causal World, Eternal World, Creator/Fork/Share and Media Demo
VNO + independent replay strengthens Independent Evidence, Experiment Engine, Novelty validation and Media Demo

akaLoop: Re-audit all 12 systems from fresh master and latest runtime/evidence.
Recompute TED_MEDIA_READINESS from machine-readable state; never copy the previous number blindly.
Find the weakest high-leverage bottleneck and identify which other systems the same implementation can strengthen.
Implement or verify one bounded real capability when safe; prefer shared contracts over one-off demos.
Update the machine-readable readiness state only for evidence-backed deltas.
End the report with the required readiness line and the strongest remaining blocker.
